reason: Both conversations ended at the correct diagnosis (dryer heater or thermal cut-out open circuit) with an engineer escalation and consistent 'unplug first' advice, and neither asked for the full model number or offered to bypass the cut-out. Conversation 1 engaged more with the interrupted-cycle clue and correctly identified the round button as the thermal cut-out, but it padded the path with unsupported checks ill-suited to a washer-dryer (a pull-out condenser image flagged as 'dryers only', then cleaning 'moisture sensor strips' that cannot explain a stone-cold drum from the start) and the misleading hint that the cut-out 'may need time to reset'. Conversation 2 recognised early that a stone-cold door glass points to an electrical heater/cut-out fault rather than airflow, reached the same honest conclusion in fewer steps, explained what the engineer would replace, and only slipped by conflating the pump filter with the lint filter. Neither proactively asked whether a cycle had been interrupted, so the edge goes to the tighter, less fabricated route.
